Your Mind is Your Prison

Most traders fail not because they do not have a system and a set of rules, but they fail from mental exhaustion - constantly looking for validations, wanting to be right, and rushing to be profitable to prove that they are a successful trader.

A real successful trader does not need a flashy PnL to prove that he is successful. He is already successful in understanding himself and his system with utmost clarity and depth. 

The market doesn't decide who he is, he enters the market only to execute his identity. Charts and PnL movements (and others' opinions) don't trigger his emotions, as he is only focusing on building results from calmly executing his edge when present. 

That's what consistency and discipline is about, from understanding, and actually doing it.

Consistency is in your mind.

I went hiking again last weekend. It was pouring rain, but the moment I reached the summit, the sky cleared up. It felt amazing, and the sunshine helped dry my soaked clothes too. That said, I hadn’t slept at all the night before, so I wasn’t feeling very well.

The reason I hadn’t slept was because I was working on something called “Breakout Health.”

I  hear people say that breakouts have been working well lately or that they’ve been failing, but I realized that I had been judging that only based on the stocks I personally watch. So I started wondering what it would look like if I actually quantified it.

Breakout Health is a score based on how stocks that had a 2nd-Pivot Break within the past 20 trading days performed after breaking their pivots.

More specifically, I assign points based on things like whether the stock avoided reaching -1R (=ADR%) within 3 days, whether it reached +1R within 5 days, whether it reached +2R within 10 days, and whether it was still above the pivot 5 days after the breakout. I then calculate a weighted average of those results to create the score.

I’m still testing it as a beta, so I wouldn’t call it finished yet, but I’m going to keep watching it for a while.

The current score is lower than I expected, so I actually think this is a good time to test it.

This is not a predictive indicator. It’s an indicator of current breakout health, so it might be worth keeping in the back of your mind when looking at the market.

April - May 2026 was the only window of opportunity to make your year while the rest of the time has, for the most part, been challenging. 

Personally, I have to admit that I've found 2026 to be a difficult trading year and have treaded water (equity curve moving sideways) during the choppy (yellow) periods. 

That said, there definitely were select opportunities during the chop that I could have handled/capitalized better. I've spent a huge part of July dwelling on it which honestly wasn't good for the mental health, but taking a step back, I've already made my year in April/May and being able to keep a chunk of those gains is what I should be grateful for.

Room for improvement? Most definitely! And that is what makes speculating in the markets so fun - the never ending quest of self-improvement. Give me a choppy period like this again and I am sure I can handle it better. Heck, give me a trending environment like 2025 (on both the upside and downside) and I am confident that I'm going to kill it.

If you're struggling at the moment, know that the name of the game now is literally survival. Protecting capital and biding time until the environment improves is planting the seed for future success.

Finance wasn't my major. English wasn't my first language. And where I come from, building a voice in the investing and trading world wasn't exactly a path I ever imagined for myself.

Outside of work, I was spending nearly 6 hours every day learning everything I could - studying technical and fundamental analysis, making mistakes, and starting all over again the next day. I didn't know where any of it would lead. I just knew I loved it and wanted to get better.

And I know I didn't get here alone. My mom is the reason I am where I am today. My brother carried me through some of the hardest moments of my life. My dad taught me to never give up. My best friend has seen every version of me since day one and always pushed me to become a better person. My mentor made me the trader and investor I am today and gave me a friendship and bond I'll forever be grateful for. And my girlfriend believed in me when I had nothing - she chose the person before any of this existed.

These are my roots. And no matter where this journey takes me, I'll never forget them.

I still have so much to learn and much bigger dreams ahead of me.If there's one thing I hope someone takes from my journey, it's this: your starting point doesn't have to decide where you end up.
